clue.text: One can blow or start to tamper with unusual safe

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, here of tamper

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or unusual
peter is underworld slang for a safe, as blown by safecrackers

explanation.surface: A safecracker is told either to blow the strange safe or at least begin fiddling with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' and 'safe' paint a safecracking scene, but 'One can blow' is the definition: a musician who blows a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass player sounds the instrument by blowing into its mouthpiece.

clue.text: Its responsibility is to land forces

definitions.text: Its responsibility is to land forces

parts.words: Its responsibility is to land forces
parts.note: reads like a military command, but describes a ship carrying soldiers ashore

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that carries troops and puts them ashore.

clue.text: Dark it is under Continental quilt

explanation.surface: Night falls under a duvet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'un lit' is French for 'a bed', which is what lies under a continental quilt or duvet.
explanation.definitionFit: Without light means dark; and a French bed, un lit, is what lies beneath a duvet.

clue.text: Standard weapon, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: Calling something a standard weapon is just a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of talking, idiom or jargon.

clue.text: Set. I fume to go off!

definitions.text: Set. I fume to go off!

indicators.note: to go off is to explode, so these letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets a bomb and seethes, waiting for it to explode.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue is definition and wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A delayed detonator, set to explode after a period.

clue.text: Cardinal achievement, to edit

parts.note: cardinal is a deep red colour
an act is a deed or achievement

explanation.surface: A cardinal's achievement is to censor the text.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare a text for publication, or black out sensitive parts.

clue.text: Sanctimonious cant rejected — given the bird

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimonious

indicators.note: rejected means the word for cant is thrown back, read right to left

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or tip

explanation.surface: A self-righteous hypocrite is booed off, given the bird by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the bird' is British slang for being jeered, but here 'the bird' is the definition. 'rejected' turns TIP into PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird of fields and moorland, related to wagtails.

clue.text: Does one position flags on side-. walks?

definitions.text: Does one position flags on side-. walks?

parts.words: Does one position flags on side-. walks?
parts.note: flags are paving stones, not banners, so the one positioning them is a pavement layer

explanation.definitionFit: A person who lays paving slabs or flagstones.

clue.text: Part of Texas seized by Cook, say?

explanation.definitionFit: The northern strip of Texas jutting up like a handle; and a cook grips the grip of a frying vessel.

clue.text: Wrong quarter of Austrian fruitcake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
E, east, is a compass quarter

explanation.surface: A slice of Austrian cake is cut wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich Central European layered cake, often with fruit.

clue.text: Crude tattoo made by West Indian music-maker?

parts.note: crude is unrefined oil
a tattoo is a rhythmic drumbeat, so a drum

explanation.surface: A rough tattoo is inked by a Caribbean musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Caribbean steel pans were first hammered out of discarded oil containers, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel bands in Trinidad make instruments from discarded petroleum barrels.

clue.text: God-given right of a dowser?

parts.note: God-given means divine, coming from heaven

explanation.surface: A water-finder claims a heaven-sent gift as a sacred right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God-given right' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-finder searches for underground springs with a forked hazel rod.

clue.text: Animal painter in ancient city

parts.note: a pet is a kept animal
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A painter of animals works among old ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock-cut Nabataean capital in Jordan, famed for its rose-red stone.

clue.text: Agent's commission from cast about to perform inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for perform goes within the word for cast about

parts.note: to cast about is to search around, to forage
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent takes a fee from the cast for getting them on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company, but 'cast about' means rummage around, giving FORAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fee a factor, or commercial agent, charges on goods handled for a principal.

clue.text: Harsh chest — the intractable sort

parts.note: harsh means hard
a chest is a case or box

explanation.surface: A harsh chest of drawers seems as stubborn as its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, incorrigible person who will not be reformed.

clue.text: Arranged parts of it are late — even the score

indicators.note: arranged parts of says the letters of the next words are reordered

explanation.surface: Parts of it arrive late, so somebody gets their own back.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay back an injury in kind, getting even.

clue.text: Reported fragrance of Continental flower

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so a word that sounds like the one for fragrance

parts.note: a fragrance is an odour

explanation.surface: A European bloom is said to give off a lovely scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows, a river: the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, and this one forms much of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Rising again, the Roman thing has top priority

parts.note: res is Latin, the Roman language, for thing
something urgent has top priority

explanation.surface: The Roman thing rising again takes precedence over all.
explanation.definitionFit: Revived, coming back up after decline.

clue.text: Be cleverer than MA tutors, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Can students outwit their MA tutors?
explanation.definitionFit: To outwit or get the better of someone.

clue.text: It entails hitting the nail on the head, and concentrating attention

definitions.text: It entails hitting the nail on the head

explanation.definitionFit: Fastening with metal pins hammered flat; and gripping, absorbing.

clue.text: Way to touch Henry?

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Is there a way of reaching out to Henry?
explanation.definitionFit: A track or route is a way.

clue.text: Kiss without getting trapped in affair

indicators.note: getting trapped in says the word for without is caught inside the word for kiss

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
sine is Latin for without

explanation.surface: Someone tries to steal a kiss without being caught up in an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a container signal but supplies SINE, Latin for without.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair in the sense of a matter or concern, as in 'a strange business'.

clue.text: Granny's first large marble kitchen?

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word Granny's

parts.note: an alley is a large playing marble

explanation.surface: Granny's first big marble-topped kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marble' suggests a worktop; it is the toy, ALLEY. The question mark: a ship's kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or aircraft's cooking area.

clue.text: This Italian barmaid left with first-class return

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: return says the letters for first-class are turned backwards

parts.note: A1 is first class, written AI

explanation.surface: An Italian barmaid leaves with a return ticket in first class.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia, an Italian heiress, appears in court disguised as a lawyer: a maid at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's heroine who pleads in court as a young lawyer, hence a woman at the bar.

clue.text: Book narrow boats to see Hawaii's outstanding features

parts.note: vol is short for volume, a book
canoes are narrow boats

explanation.surface: A tourist books canal boats to tour the sights of Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: 'narrow boats' suggests British canal barges; here it just means slim craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauna Loa and Kilauea are the islands' dominating peaks, standing out above the landscape.

clue.text: He may be collared for some of the civic arrangements

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man may be arrested for some of the town's arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collared' suggests arrest; it is the clerical dog collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman wears a white dog collar.

clue.text: One would not need much jelly!

definitions.text: One would not need much jelly!

parts.words: One would not need much jelly!
parts.note: jellied eels are a London dish; a tiny young eel would need very little jelly to set it

explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a traditional East London dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel, so small it would need only a little aspic.

clue.text: Bowed lady

explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument played with a bow; and a girl's name, the heroine of Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Floral head-dress to keep quiet in: Swiss Cottage?

indicators.note: to keep here means to hold within, so the cottage holds the letter for quiet

parts.note: a chalet is a Swiss cottage
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A garland is worn to keep things calm at Swiss Cottage, a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a London district, but here it is literally a cottage in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath or garland of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: Stout advert I model for

parts.note: to model is to pose

explanation.surface: A stout ad has a model posing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' suggests the beer of an advert, but it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatty, hence plump or corpulent.

clue.text: Syrinx-like, abounding in marsh grass

explanation.definitionFit: Syrinx was a nymph turned into rushes, and a syrinx is a pan pipe with a thin piping tone; marshes full of tall rushes are thick with stems.

clue.text: One's own tissue-transplant — personally signed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said out loud, giving a similar sound

parts.note: a thing personally signed is autographed

explanation.surface: A patient's own skin graft comes with a signed certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A graft taken from one part of a patient's body to another of the same body.
